app.q: Do my customers need to install an app?
app.a: No. They scan the QR code with the phone camera and everything happens in the browser. iPhone users can add the order page to their Home Screen to receive notifications, which takes three taps and is optional.

iphone.q: Does the ring work on iPhone?
iphone.a: Yes, with a limit Apple sets: notifications only reach web pages added to the Home Screen (iOS 16.4 and later). Without that, the iPhone rings with a full-screen alert and sound while the order page is open, and the page keeps the screen awake. We show customers which case applies to their phone.

internet.q: What if the connection is bad?
internet.a: The order page is light and keeps checking for updates every few seconds when the live connection drops, so a ready order still reaches the customer. The board works the same way at the counter.

payment.a: Not in this version. Customers pay at the counter as they do today; the order shows the total. You pay only your monthly subscription, never a commission on orders.

hardware.a: A tablet or phone with a browser at the counter, and a printer for the QR codes (any office printer, or a print shop). A TV for the call-out screen is optional.

languages.a: Arabic, French and English, everywhere: your menu, the customer pages and your dashboard. Arabic is laid out right to left. You choose which languages your shop page offers.

data.q: What do you keep about my customers?
data.a: A first name or nickname for calling the order, and an optional phone number used only for the fallback alert. Phone numbers are erased automatically after the period you set (30 days by default). We never sell data or show ads.

cancel.q: Can I stop at any time?
cancel.a: Yes. Cancel from the billing page; your shop stays active until the end of the period you paid for. There is no long contract.

legal.draft: Draft for legal review. These texts follow Algerian law as we understand it (Law 18-07 on personal data, as amended by Law 25-11; Law 18-05 on electronic commerce; Law 09-03 on consumer protection). The bracketed items are the operator’s own details and filings. An Algerian lawyer must check them before launch.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.intro: These terms govern the use of {brand}, a service that lets restaurants, cafés and food businesses in Algeria take orders through QR codes and call customers when their order is ready. By creating a shop you accept them on behalf of your business.

p: {brand} is operated by [operator legal name], [legal form], registered in the commercial register under n° [RC number], tax identification number (NIF) [NIF], statistical number (NIS) [NIS], article of taxation (AI) [AI], whose registered office is at [address], Algeria. You can reach us at [support email] or [phone].

sections.h: The service and who it is for
p: {brand} provides a shop page and menu, QR codes to print, an order board, alerts that tell customers their order is ready, and the related dashboard. It is a business service for food businesses. It is not a marketplace: orders are placed with your shop, and food is paid for at your counter, outside the service.
Alerts depend on each customer’s phone, browser and settings. We describe their limits in the product and do not guarantee that every alert reaches every customer.
You must give accurate information and keep your password safe. You are responsible for what happens under your account, including the staff accounts you create.
You confirm that you are authorised to act for the business you register and that it may lawfully sell what your menu offers.

Packs, prices and allowances are shown on the pricing page and in your dashboard, in Algerian dinars. A pack starts with a free period; the subscription period then runs from your confirmed payment for the length stated (for example one year). Nothing is charged automatically.

We issue an invoice for each payment with the mentions required by Algerian law. If a period ends unpaid, your shop enters a grace period and is then suspended until you pay; your data is kept. You can cancel at any time: the shop stays active until the end of the period you paid for. Paid periods are not refunded except where the law requires it.

You are the seller to your customers. You are responsible for your menu, your prices (displayed in dinars, taxes included where applicable), the information you give about your food, including allergens and ingredients, hygiene and food safety, and for complying with the laws that apply to your sales, in particular Law 18-05 on electronic commerce and Law 09-03 on consumer protection.
You must not sell through the service anything that the law prohibits from being sold online.

sections.h: Your content and your customers’ data
p: You keep all rights to your menu, photos, logo and other content, and allow us to host and display them to provide the service.
For your customers’ order data you are the data controller and we process it on your behalf. Our Privacy notice explains this and how to exercise rights.
Do not use the service for anything unlawful, to collect data you are not entitled to, to send unsolicited messages, or to disrupt or probe the service. We may suspend accounts that do.

We work to keep the service available but do not promise it will be uninterrupted. To the extent the law allows, our liability is limited to the amount you paid us in the twelve months before the event giving rise to the claim, and we are not liable for indirect losses such as lost profits. Nothing here limits liability that cannot be limited by law.

We may update these terms and will tell you in advance of material changes. You may close your account at any time. We may end the service for an account that breaches these terms, after notice when possible. After closure, we keep invoices for the period the law requires and delete the rest.
These terms are available in Arabic, French and English; the Arabic version prevails if they differ.
They are governed by Algerian law. Disputes are brought before the competent courts of [city], Algeria, after an attempt to settle them amicably.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: This notice explains what personal data {brand} handles, why, and for how long, under Algerian Law n° 18-07 on the protection of natural persons in the processing of personal data (as amended and supplemented, notably by Law n° 25-11). It covers shop owners and staff, and customers who order from shops using {brand}.

p: For shop accounts (owners and staff), [operator legal name] (see the Terms) is the data controller.
For customers’ orders, the shop is the data controller and [operator legal name] processes the data on the shop’s behalf, only to run the service.

Customers: the name or nickname you enter, your order, its time and number, the table if you scanned a table code, and, only if you choose to give it, a phone number. If you allow notifications, your browser gives us a push address for that order.
Shop owners and staff: email, password (stored only as a secure hash by our authentication provider), shop details, menu, staff invitations, invoices, payments and uploaded receipts.
We do not collect national ID numbers, payment card numbers (card payments for subscriptions happen on the payment provider’s page), location, or any sensitive data.

To take and show orders and to tell you when your order is ready (necessary to perform the order you place); to run accounts and billing (performance of the subscription contract and legal obligations); to keep the service secure, for example by limiting repeated sign-in or order attempts (legitimate interest).

Your phone number and your notification permission rest on your consent. They are optional, and you can withdraw consent at any time by clearing the phone number from your order next time, blocking notifications in your browser, or contacting the shop or us.
We do not sell data, use it for advertising, or profile customers.

The processing described here is declared to the National Authority for the Protection of Personal Data (ANPDP) under Law 18-07: [ANPDP receipt or authorisation reference]. The authority’s site is anpdp.dz.

The service is hosted with Supabase (database, authentication, storage) and Vercel (application servers), whose servers are located outside Algeria: [region, e.g. Paris, France]. Payment for subscriptions is handled by Chargily Pay; email is sent through [email provider]; if a shop enables SMS or WhatsApp fallback alerts, through [messaging provider].

Under Law 18-07, a transfer of personal data abroad requires the authorisation of the ANPDP and an adequate level of protection in the receiving country. [Authorisation reference]. Each provider processes data only to deliver its part of the service and under contractual confidentiality and security commitments.

Data is kept no longer than needed for its purpose. Customer phone numbers are erased automatically after the period the shop sets (30 days by default, at most one year). Push addresses are deleted a day after the order is closed. Orders are kept for the shop’s history and accounting.
Account data is kept while the account is active. Invoices and accounting records are kept for the period the law requires ([10 years] under the Commercial Code, to be confirmed by your accountant).

Under Law 18-07 you have the right to be informed, to access your data, to have it corrected, and to object to its processing for legitimate reasons. Contact the shop you ordered from, or us at [privacy contact email]; we answer within one month.
If you are not satisfied, you may complain to the ANPDP (anpdp.dz).

Data is encrypted in transit, each shop’s data is isolated from every other shop’s, staff see only orders, order links use long random codes, and sign-in and ordering are rate-limited. No system is perfectly secure: we will notify the authority and the people concerned of a breach within the period the law sets.
The service is not aimed at children. Where a minor orders, the consent of a parent or legal representative is required for the optional data (phone number, notifications).

We use only what the service needs: a sign-in cookie for shop owners and staff, a language preference, and storage on the customer’s own device that remembers their ticket and recent orders. No advertising or tracking cookies.
